questions: Are TREND_INGEST_ENABLED and TREND_INGEST_CLASSIFIER_WORKSPACE_ID actually set to a non-blank/true value in any committed .env or docker-compose file for any environment, or do they remain false/blank everywhere in the RC?
Does TrendPullJob.pullTrends() actually short-circuit before writing any row when hasClassifierWorkspaceId() is false, and can a real test run reproduce written=0 for that path?

Is TrendPullJob's fail-closed, disabled-by-default state a deliberate, documented, already-escalated business decision (per its own class javadoc) rather than an accidental defect, and does that change how it should be scored versus a normal P1 'broken flow'?

What is the exact character length of the scoped idempotency key WalletService.requestCreatorWithdrawal builds ('creator-withdraw:' + userId + ':' + client idempotencyKey), and does it exceed wallet_transactions.idempotency_key / payouts.idempotency_key's committed VARCHAR(64) definition?

Does IdempotencyService's own 128-char reservation-key guard (added for a documented, different overflow on idempotency_keys.idempotency_key VARCHAR(128)) actually protect the separate, smaller VARCHAR(64) columns that WalletLedgerService and PayoutRepository write scopedKey into, or is that a distinct, unprotected code path?
Are WalletServiceTest and WalletLedgerServiceTest real database-backed tests, or pure Mockito mocks structurally incapable of observing a MySQL 'Data too long for column' failure?

Is MySQL's default STRICT_TRANS_TABLES sql_mode actually the operative mode for this deployment (is there any override to a non-strict mode anywhere in config), and under it does an INSERT exceeding a VARCHAR(64) column throw rather than silently truncate?
Does EscrowService.refundInternal() check any deliverable/milestone approval or posting state before allowing a refund, or only workspace ownership + hold status FUNDED + the dispute-freeze guard?

What is the only value ever assigned to PaymentMilestone.releaseCondition across the whole codebase, and does that create a window where a hold stays FUNDED after a deliverable reaches APPROVED but before it reaches POSTED?

Is POST /escrow/refund actually reachable by an ordinary brand OWNER/ADMIN using the standard brand JWT/session (the same auth every other brand action uses), or does it require some elevated/internal-only credential the frontend does not expose?

Does EscrowController's own javadoc/policy citation (escrow-and-refund-policy.md §3: 'funds move ONLY through release or a dispute-resolution outcome, with no on-demand refund') contradict what the implementation actually permits, and does that strengthen or weaken the finding?
Is there any existing unit or integration test that exercises 'brand refunds an APPROVED-but-not-yet-POSTED milestone' and asserts it is blocked?
Could an automatic release-on-approval path realistically close this window in the common case, reducing real-world exploitability of EV-015?
Are the cited line numbers for all three findings accurate against the actual clean 115f698 checkout, or has the code moved/changed since the finder read it?
For each finding, does the verification evidence come from the clean RC checkout only, or does any of it inadvertently rely on the uncommitted working tree?

verdicts.title: TrendPullJob ships disabled and fails closed without TREND_INGEST_CLASSIFIER_WORKSPACE_ID; zero automated trend ingestion in production
verdicts.reason: Read TrendPullJob.java:191-289 in the clean RC: pullTrends() returns immediately if !props.isEnabled() (line 194-197), and even when enabled, every candidate that passes the word filter is rejected at line 281 ('classifier_unconfigured') and counted, never written, whenever !props.hasClassifierWorkspaceId(). Read TrendIngestProperties.java:25-27,67,173-175: enabled defaults to false and classifierWorkspaceId defaults to "" (hasClassifierWorkspaceId() false). Read application.yml:569-577: `trend-ingest.enabled: ${TREND_INGEST_ENABLED:false}` and `classifier-workspace-id: ${TREND_INGEST_CLASSIFIER_WORKSPACE_ID:}` -- both bindings match the finding's cited lines exactly. Grepped all three committed compose files (deploy/hostinger/docker-compose.hostinger.yml:212,228; deploy/utho/docker-compose.utho.yml:213,247; deploy/utho/docker-compose.utho-shared.yml:241,275) -- all pass these through with the SAME blank/false shell defaults (`${VAR:-false}` / `${VAR:-}`), never a literal value. Grepped .env.production and .env.local.example for TREND_INGEST -- zero matches, confirming no committed environment file overrides either default. Executed `mvn -q -o -Dtest=TrendIngestConfigWiringTest,TrendPullJobTest test` from the RC's influora-api directory: exit code 0, and the captured log shows the exact runtime behavior the finding describes, e.g. 'TrendPullJob: rejected id=... reason=classifier_unconfigured -- no influora.trend-ingest.classifier-workspace-id set, failing closed' followed by 'written=0', and a separate 'TrendPullJob: disabled (influora.trend-ingest.enabled=false), skipping run' log line -- this is a real, green, passing test run directly exercising both fail-closed branches, not a hypothesis. One correction to the original claim's framing: this is not an accidental defect -- the class javadoc (lines 60-64) explicitly documents it as an escalated, undecided business question (who pays for the AI classifier call) rather than a silent bug, and dev/blueprint-meera-ai's P1/P2 disagreement is legitimate given that framing. I side with P1 over P2 because TrendSpark ingestion is a previously-reported, already-built feature (project_trendspark_build_state.md) that is completely and permanently non-functional in every committed environment with no operator alert -- that is a go-live-relevant gap for that feature even though it fails safe rather than fails loud.
verdicts.new_evidence: Ran the cited TrendPullJobTest/TrendIngestConfigWiringTest suite against the clean RC (mvn -q -o -Dtest=TrendIngestConfigWiringTest,TrendPullJobTest test): BUILD exit 0, and the captured log directly shows the classifier_unconfigured fail-closed branch executing with written=0, plus the enabled=false skip branch -- upgrading this from static analysis to runtime-observed behavior. Confirmed via grep that all three committed docker-compose files and both committed .env files leave TREND_INGEST_ENABLED/TREND_INGEST_CLASSIFIER_WORKSPACE_ID at their blank/false shell defaults, with no override found anywhere in the RC.

verdicts.title: Creator withdrawal idempotency key (80/82 chars) overflows VARCHAR(64) in wallet_transactions and payouts: every FE withdrawal fails at commit
verdicts.reason: Read WalletService.java:304: scopedKey = "creator-withdraw:" + userId + ":" + idempotencyKey. Confirmed userId is a ULID: V1 migration defines `users.id VARCHAR(26)` and Ulids.newUlid() (com.influora.common.Ulids) wraps UlidCreator, which emits the standard 26-character ULID. Confirmed idempotencyKey is a standard UUID: src/pages/creator-wallet.tsx:591 mints it via `safeRandomUUID()` (36 chars incl. hyphens) client-side, once per submission, and sends it as the Idempotency-Key header consumed unmodified at WalletController.java:117-124 and WalletService.java:250-254 (only null/blank-checked, never length-checked). Arithmetic: 'creator-withdraw:' (17 chars) + 26-char userId + ':' (1) + 36-char UUID = 80 chars for the payouts-table key (Payout.createQueued at WalletService.java:~395 stores this scopedKey verbatim); WalletLedgerService.java:158,176 appends ':D'/':C' to the SAME scopedKey for the two wallet_transactions legs, producing 82 chars -- this exactly matches the finder's claimed 80/82. Read V8__wallet_transactions.sql:15 (`idempotency_key VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL ... UNIQUE`) and V48__payouts.sql:13 (`idempotency_key VARCHAR(64) ... NOT NULL UNIQUE`) -- both committed migrations confirm the 64-char ceiling. Checked whether IdempotencyService's own length guard (validateReservationKeyLength, MAX_RESERVATION_KEY_LENGTH=128, IdempotencyService.java:80,225-235) would catch this first: it composes a DIFFERENT, longer key ('wallet.withdraw:' + userId + ':' + scopedKey ~ 123 chars) against idempotency_keys.idempotency_key VARCHAR(128) -- 123<128, so that guard passes and does NOT protect the separate, smaller wallet_transactions/payouts VARCHAR(64) columns scopedKey is written into afterward inside doProcessWithdrawal. Confirmed WalletServiceTest.java:60-83 and WalletLedgerServiceTest.java:25-32 are both pure @ExtendWith(MockitoExtension.class) with every repository @Mock -- neither can execute a real INSERT and so neither could ever observe this DB-level overflow, matching the known 'Mockito tests skip schema validation' pattern in this codebase. Confirmed sql_mode STRICT_TRANS_TABLES is the codebase's own stated operative mode (referenced in V20260907120000__ai_conversations_tenant_type.sql:40) with no override to a lenient mode found anywhere in deploy/ or application*.yml, so a real MySQL insert of an 80/82-char value into VARCHAR(64) would raise a 'Data too long for column' error rather than silently truncate. WalletLedgerService.post's catch(DataIntegrityViolationException) block (lines 186-199) would then find no existing posting under the (unwritten) key and throw ApiException('LEDGER_POSTING_CONFLICT', 409) -- so in practice every real creator withdrawal fails with a misleading 409 rather than a 500, but it still fails 100% of the time as claimed. I did not execute a live MySQL/Testcontainers reproduction (none run locally without Docker per this repo's own known constraint), so I stop short of CONFIRMED-RUNTIME, but the character-length match is exact and every mitigating mechanism I checked (the 128-char guard, the Mockito test suite) fails to cover this specific write path.
verdicts.new_evidence: Recomputed the exact scoped-key length from the RC's own code (80 chars for payouts, 82 for wallet_transactions legs) and matched it precisely against the committed VARCHAR(64) DDL in V8__wallet_transactions.sql and V48__payouts.sql. Traced IdempotencyService's existing 128-char guard and showed it composes a different, longer key against a different (128-char) column and therefore does not protect this write path. Confirmed both WalletServiceTest and WalletLedgerServiceTest are fully Mockito-mocked and structurally cannot catch this.

verdicts.title: Brand OWNER/ADMIN can refund a FUNDED escrow hold to itself on demand, even after delivery/approval, bypassing dispute resolution
verdicts.reason: Read EscrowService.java:943-1013 (refundInternal): the only gates are workspace-ownership match (line 972), hold.getStatus()==REFUNDED idempotent no-op (975-977), assertEscrowNotBlockedByDispute on the linked collaboration if one resolves (981-985, defined at 1804-1810 -- checks only CollaborationStatus.DISPUTED or an active Dispute row), and requireStatus(hold, FUNDED) (987). There is no check anywhere in this method of milestone status, deliverable status, or whether the creator's work was ever submitted/approved. Confirmed this is not merely a theoretical gap: MilestoneStatus.java has no APPROVED value at all (approval lives on Deliverable, not PaymentMilestone), and BrandDeliverableService.approve() (lines 129-207) only ATTEMPTS an escrow release via tryReleaseOnApproval, gated by assertReleaseConditionSatisfied (EscrowService.java:1545-1585), which reads the milestone's release_condition -- defaulting to ReleaseCondition.ON_POSTED when unset (line 1576). Grepped every ReleaseCondition assignment in main source: PaymentMilestone.java:249 is the ONLY place a milestone's releaseCondition is ever set, and it hard-codes ON_POSTED -- there is no code path anywhere that creates a milestone with any other release_condition. This means EVERY milestone in this system requires the deliverable to reach POSTED (not just APPROVED) before tryReleaseOnApproval will actually move money, so approving a deliverable routinely leaves its hold FUNDED. In that always-present window, a brand OWNER/ADMIN can call POST /escrow/refund directly (EscrowController.java:151-165, gated only by the same brandContext.requireBrandWorkspace + requireRole(OWNER,ADMIN) used for every other ordinary brand action -- no elevated/internal-only credential) and get its money back despite the creator's work having already been approved, with no dispute ever filed. Critically, EscrowController.java:140-148's own javadoc states the product POLICY is 'funds move ONLY through release or a dispute-resolution outcome, with no on-demand refund' and that 'the refund a brand can actually reach in product runs through DisputeService.resolve -> EscrowService.adminRefundForDispute, not here' -- i.e., the team's own documented intent is that this exact self-service refund should NOT be brand-reachable, yet the code enforces that intent only by omitting a frontend button, not with any server-side control (no ops-only role check, no internal network restriction, no feature flag). Grepped EscrowServiceTest.java for any refund-after-approval test -- none exists (only refundStillSucceedsOnCancelledCollaboration and dispute-related refund tests). Given (a) this is the default and only behavior for 100% of milestones (not a rare edge case), (b) it is trivially reachable by any authenticated brand user via a plain API call with no additional barrier, (c) it directly contradicts the platform's own stated payment-protection policy, and (d) it produces direct, repeatable financial harm to creators (denial of payment for approved work) rather than merely a broken/unreliable flow, I upgrade this from the finder's P1 to P0 (financial/security category) rather than downgrading it -- the original P1 rating understates a defect that is fully committed, always-present, and directly monetizable against creators.
verdicts.new_evidence: Traced PaymentMilestone.java:249 as the SOLE assignment site for ReleaseCondition anywhere in main source, confirming ON_POSTED is universal, not a corner case -- this converts the 'even after approval' scenario from a hypothetical into the default behavior for every milestone. Read EscrowController.java:140-148's javadoc, which shows the code comment itself documents the exact policy this implementation violates ('no on-demand refund'), and confirmed the refund endpoint's auth check is identical to ordinary brand actions (no elevated gate). Confirmed no existing test covers 'refund after approval but before posting'.
